name: Orly Enrique Apolo-Apolo
roleLines: Founder, Agrocoding · Chief AI Consultant, Planticus
tagline: AI, hyperspectral imaging and remote sensing for agri-food systems.
address: Parc Científic i Tecnològic Agroalimentari de Lleida
bio: I'm a researcher working at the intersection of AI, hyperspectral imaging and remote sensing for agri-food systems — from UAV and satellite crop monitoring to computer vision for fruit quality, using deep learning methods built for the noisy, high-dimensional data typical of field and postharvest environments.

I completed my Ph.D. at the University of Seville and a postdoc at KU Leuven on hyperspectral detection of Fusarium head blight. I now work in the Postharvest programme at IRTA–Fruitcentre in Lleida, detecting fruit disorders before they become visible, while also running Agrocoding and advising Planticus as Chief AI Consultant.

researchAreas.title: Hyperspectral & multispectral imaging
researchAreas.description: Push-broom and snapshot imaging systems for detecting disease, quality traits and physiological disorders that aren't visible to the eye or a standard camera.

researchAreas.title: UAV & satellite remote sensing
researchAreas.description: Drone-based yield and canopy estimation, and Sentinel-2 / Planet / ERA5 data fusion for orchard and landscape-scale monitoring.

researchAreas.title: Deep learning for agri-food
researchAreas.description: CNNs, GANs, vision transformers and SAM-based segmentation, adapted to the scale, noise and label scarcity typical of field and postharvest data.

researchAreas.title: Postharvest quality & disorders
researchAreas.description: Non-destructive, pre-symptomatic detection of fruit disorders, connecting sensing methods to real packing-house and storage workflows.

education.detail: AI, drones and remote sensing for precision agriculture. Six-month research stay at Wageningen University & Research (Netherlands) on drone-based yield estimation. PIF Fellowship. Award-winning doctoral thesis, Spain/Portugal 2022–2023.
Both completed with extraordinary end-of-studies distinction.

experience.detail: Non-destructive sensing and AI for pre-symptomatic detection of postharvest fruit disorders.
Applied AI for agronomy and postharvest operations.
Digitalization and AI tools for agri-food applications.

Hyperspectral detection of Fusarium head blight with a tractor-mounted push-broom camera; generative adversarial networks and satellite imagery for vegetation change under climate change. Fieldwork in Belgium and Lithuania.
Ph.D. research and early postdoctoral work on UAV-based precision agriculture, including an internship at IFAPA.
